skill.name: commit-chat-push
skill.description: Guides Codex through reviewing repository changes, invoking a referenced session exporter, checking transcript privacy, staging selected files, committing, and pushing.
skill.summary: Commit repository changes with a reviewed Codex session transcript and push the current branch.
skill.author: bertona88

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, safe Git inspection commands, and defensive secret-search patterns. Confirmed risks include reading private Codex sessions, permitting raw-session commits, and pushing transcript content to a remote repository. The referenced redaction exporter is missing, so its privacy controls cannot be audited.

remediation.issue: The security-critical transcript exporter is missing from the audited package.
remediation.suggestion: Include the exporter source and tests. Verify secret redaction, anchored session selection, path handling, and safe output defaults before publication.

remediation.issue: The workflow permits raw Codex session logs to be committed after a warning.
remediation.suggestion: Prohibit raw JSONL commits. Export only reviewed Markdown with system instructions, tool output, local paths, and secret patterns removed.

remediation.issue: Transcript content is pushed to a remote repository.
remediation.suggestion: Show the selected remote, staged transcript, and secret-scan result. Require explicit confirmation immediately before push.

remediation.issue: Unanchored selection can choose the newest session sharing the repository path.
remediation.suggestion: Require a fresh unique anchor for every export. Remove automatic newest-session fallback from the publish workflow.

content.user_title: Commit Code With a Reviewed Codex Transcript
content.value_statement: Implementation context is often lost after code is committed. This workflow guides transcript review, selective staging, commit creation, and branch publication.
actual_capabilities: Guides repository inspection with Git status, remote, branch, and diff commands.
Requests focused tests or checks before creating a commit.
Defines an anchor-based procedure for selecting a Codex session.
Guides transcript review and secret scanning before staging.
Uses explicit pathspecs and staged diffs to limit committed files.
Guides normal upstream pushes and warns against unrequested force pushes.
limitations: The referenced transcript exporter is not included in the audited package.
Redaction cannot guarantee removal of every secret or private message.
The workflow requires Git, Python, ripgrep, and accessible local Codex sessions.
A push publishes the reviewed transcript to the configured repository remote.

use_cases.title: Preserve Feature Provenance
use_cases.description: Commit a reviewed implementation transcript beside a completed feature for future maintenance.

use_cases.title: Document Assisted Changes
use_cases.description: Record selected development context for reviewers who need to understand how a change was produced.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Handoffs
use_cases.description: Apply consistent checks before staging code, attaching a transcript, creating a commit, and pushing.

prompt_templates.title: Commit Completed Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use commit-chat-push to review my current changes, include a redacted Codex transcript, commit the intended files, and push the branch.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants the standard workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Commit With Focused Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the diff, run the narrowest relevant tests, export the anchored session, scan it for secrets, then commit and push.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants verification before publication.

prompt_templates.title: Respect Existing Transcript Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Find this repository's transcript convention, export the current anchored session there, exclude unrelated changes, show the staged diff, then commit and push.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer works in an established repository.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Controlled Provenance Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the remote and upstream, verify the change, review the redacted transcript, stage explicit paths, summarize exposure risks, request confirmation, then push.
prompt_templates.scenario: A release engineer needs tighter publication control.

output_examples.input: Include provenance, but do not expose command output.
output_examples.output: Prepared the transcript with command output omitted, reviewed it for sensitive text, and included it with the selected changes.

output_examples.input: The branch has no upstream. Publish the reviewed commit.
output_examples.output: Verified the configured remote, created the commit, established the branch upstream, and reported the push result.

best_practices: Review the selected transcript and staged diff immediately before committing.
Keep command output disabled unless every included result has been checked.
Confirm the destination remote and branch before publishing transcript content.
anti_patterns: Do not stage every dirty file when unrelated changes are present.
Do not commit raw Codex session JSONL files.
Do not force-push unless the user explicitly requests and understands it.

faq.question: What does this skill add to a commit?
faq.answer: It guides adding selected repository changes and a reviewed Markdown transcript of the Codex session.

faq.question: Does it include the transcript exporter?
faq.answer: No. The audited package references an exporter script, but that script is absent.

faq.question: Can transcript redaction remove every secret?
faq.answer: No. The documentation requires manual review and a secret scan before committing.

faq.question: How does it choose the current session?
faq.answer: The documented workflow creates a unique anchor and requires the selected session to contain it.

faq.question: Will it commit unrelated working-tree changes?
faq.answer: The instructions require explicit pathspecs and staged-diff review when unrelated changes exist.

faq.question: Does it force-push rejected changes?
faq.answer: No. It directs normal synchronization and requires an explicit user request before any force push.
